title: Rename some functions and types for endpoint tables.
description:
The "conversation table" mechanism supports two types of tables, one for
the "Conversations" menu item under "Statistics" and one for the
"Endpoints" menu item under "Statistics".  The first of them shows
statistics for conversations at various layers of the networking stack;
the second of them shows statistics for endpoints at various layers of
the networking stack.

The latter is *not* a table of hosts; an endpoint might be a host,
identified by an address at some network level (MAC, IP, etc.), or it
might be a port on a host, identified by an address/port pair.

Some data types, function names, etc. use "host" or "hostlist" or other
terms that imply that an endpoint is a host; change them to speak of
endpoints rather than hosts, using names similar to the corresponding
functions for conversations.

Provide wrapper functions and typedefs for backwards source and binary
compatibility; mark them as deprecated in favor of the new names.

Clean up some comment errors found in the process.

The "conversation table" mechanism should, ideally, be able to support showing conversations of the "virtual circuit id" type in addition to the address (and optionally port) type. Confusingly, those are called "endpoints" (like "conversation_set_endpoint_by_id"), even though they are more conversation/circuit identifiers.

> The "conversation table" mechanism should, ideally, be able to support showing conversations of the "virtual circuit id" type in addition to the address (and optionally port) type.

Yes.

However, it could only show individual endpoints of those conversations if it could identify them.  For conversations with known endpoints, e.g. address or address and port, the endpoints can be identified; however, for virtual circuits identified by a circuit ID, the endpoints could only be identified if they're known from some other source.  For example, if the call setup packets for a switched virtual circuit are available the endpoints could be shown, with statistics for a given endpoint showing traffic for all virtual circuits involving that endpoint.

> Confusingly, those are called "endpoints" (like "conversation_set_endpoint_by_id"), even though they are more conversation/circuit identifiers.

They shouldn't be.  Two address/port pairs identify a TCP or UDP conversation, but those are two separate endpoints; a circuit ID identifies conversations such as X.25 conversations, but it's not an endpoint.  What identifies a conversation is a "conversation key" or a "conversation identifier" or a "conversation tag" or something such as that.

>  For conversations with known endpoints, e.g. address or address and port, the endpoints can be identified; however, for virtual circuits identified by a circuit ID, the endpoints could only be identified if they're known from some other source. For example, if the call setup packets for a switched virtual circuit are available the endpoints could be shown, with statistics for a given endpoint showing traffic for all virtual circuits involving that endpoint.

One such case is QUIC, where there are connection IDs, and different connections can share the same UDP/IP 5-tuple, and also a connection can migrate from one 5-tuple to another. A user might want to display all traffic on the connection (presumably in the "Conversations" table) across migrations, as well as all traffic on that connection for a given 5-tuple. (And in the "Endpoints" table presumably something similar for one side of the connection.)
